title: Calprotectin
desc: Calprotectin is an abundant neutrophil protein complex (an S100A8/S100A9 heterodimer) that helps defend the host by sequestering manganese and zinc from microbes, and is measured in stool as a biomarker of gut inflammation.

title: Dissimilatory Metal Reduction
desc: Dissimilatory metal reduction is a form of anaerobic microbial respiration in which cells conserve energy by transferring respiratory electrons onto an oxidized metal, such as Fe(III), Mn(IV), or U(VI), used as the terminal electron acceptor.

title: Irving–Williams Series
desc: The Irving–Williams series is the empirical order of thermodynamic stability for high-spin divalent first-row transition-metal complexes, Mn(II) < Fe(II) < Co(II) < Ni(II) < Cu(II) > Zn(II), which holds regardless of the ligand.

title: Metal Intoxication
desc: Metal intoxication is the offensive arm of nutritional immunity in which host immune cells flood a trapped microbe with toxic excess copper and zinc to mismetalate its enzymes and destroy iron-sulfur clusters.

title: Metal Sparing
desc: Metal sparing is the remodeling of a microbe's proteome during metal starvation, in which metal-requiring proteins are replaced by isozymes that use a different metal or no metal at all, thereby reducing cellular demand for the scarce element.

title: Metallochaperone
desc: A metallochaperone is a soluble intracellular carrier protein that binds a specific metal ion and delivers it by direct protein-protein contact to a designated target enzyme or transporter.

title: Metallome
desc: The metallome is the entirety of metal and metalloid species within a cell or organism, comprising free ions together with all metal- and metalloid-containing biomolecules.

title: Metallomics
desc: Metallomics is the integrated study of the metallome — the identity, quantity, distribution, coordination chemistry and biological function of all metals and metalloids in a cell, tissue or organism.

title: Metallophore
desc: A metallophore is a low-molecular-weight molecule secreted by microorganisms to bind and acquire a specific scarce metal ion from the environment or host.

title: Metalloproteome
desc: The metalloproteome is the complete set of metal-binding proteins in an organism or cell, encompassing every protein that requires a metal ion or metal cofactor for its structure or function.

title: Metalloregulation
desc: Metalloregulation is the process by which cells sense intracellular metal-ion concentrations through metal-responsive regulatory proteins that switch target genes on or off to maintain metal homeostasis.

title: Metallostasis
desc: Metallostasis is the coordinated sensing, buffering, trafficking, and sparing of metal ions that keeps each essential metal's bioavailability within a narrow physiological range inside a cell.

title: Mismetallation
desc: Mismetallation is the binding of a metalloprotein's metal site by the wrong metal ion — usually a more competitive one — which inactivates or misdirects the enzyme.

title: Nutritional Immunity
desc: Nutritional immunity is the host defense strategy of controlling transition-metal availability—withholding iron, zinc, and manganese or intoxicating microbes with copper and zinc—to limit the growth of invading pathogens.

title: Siderophore
desc: A siderophore is a small, high-affinity iron(III)-chelating molecule that microbes secrete to scavenge scarce environmental iron and import it into the cell.

title: Six Decades of Fertilizer Use Built a Legacy of Cadmium, Nickel, and Lead in Soils and Diets
desc: A food metallomics review (1960–2025) showing how phosphate and urea fertilizers loaded soils, crops, and diets with cadmium, nickel, lead, and chromium.

title: Heavy Metals and Microbial Metallomics: A New Framework for the US Obesity Epidemic
desc: How dietary cadmium, arsenic, lead, and nickel may disrupt gut microbial metallomics—driving dysbiosis, inflammation, and insulin resistance behind obesity.

title: Concentration-Based Heavy Metal Standards to Reduce Real Exposure in Infant and Child Foods
desc: HMTc 2026 sets concentration-based, as-sold action levels for lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury, nickel and other heavy metals in infant and child foods.

title: A Unified Model for FIP-Associated Gingivitis in Cats: Disrupting Microbial Shielding and Restoring Nutritional Immunity
desc: How itraconazole and lactoferrin may treat FIP-linked gingivitis in cats by disrupting polymicrobial biofilms and restoring metal-based nutritional immunity.

title: The MC1R–Parkinson's Link May Be a Metallomic Story, Not a Cosmetic One
desc: A hypothesis linking MC1R red-hair variants to Parkinson's risk via melanin-metal chemistry: how copper, zinc, and iron shape neuromelanin's redox buffering.

title: Developmental Readiness Is Not Toxicokinetic Safety: Heavy Metals in Vegetable-Based Baby Foods
desc: Developmental readiness for solids does not ensure toxicokinetic safety: leafy greens, brassicas and root crops concentrate lead, cadmium and arsenic in baby foods.

title: Parkinson's Disease as a Disorder of Metal Dyshomeostasis Amplified by Microbial Ecology
desc: A synthesis framework proposing Parkinson's disease begins with heavy-metal dyshomeostasis that drives ferroptosis, gut dysbiosis, and α-synuclein pathology.

title: Microbiome Medicine Journal: Restoring Causal Structure to Disease Through Microbial Metallomics
desc: Microbiome Medicine Journal Vol. I sets out a mechanism-first framework linking microbial ecology, host metallome regulation, and metal dyshomeostasis to disease.

title: Nickel as a Catalytic Driver of Necrotizing Enterocolitis
desc: Dietary nickel in infant formula may activate nickel-dependent microbial enzymes (urease, glyoxalase I) that drive necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm infants.

title: From Dysbiosis to Dyshomeostasis: Reframing Parkinson's Through a Metallomic–Microbiome Lens
desc: A metallomics framework reframes Parkinson's as metal dyshomeostasis: iron, manganese, copper, zinc and nickel dysregulation drives dysbiosis and neuron loss.

title: Arsenic and the Gut Microbiome: A Two-Way Street
desc: Arsenic reshapes the gut microbiome, and gut bacteria shape arsenic's toxicity in return. See the bidirectional evidence linking metals, microbes, and disease.

title: Cadmium and the Gut Microbiome: A Hidden Route to Metabolic Disease
desc: Cadmium reshapes the gut microbiome, depletes Lachnospiraceae, weakens the gut barrier, and is linked to hepatic and metabolic dysfunction. An evidence review.

title: Feeding the Enemy: How Dietary Iron Reshapes the Gut Microbiome and Raises Enteric Infection Risk
desc: Unabsorbed dietary and supplemental iron feeds gut enteropathogens like E. coli, Salmonella and Shigella, raising inflammation and diarrhea risk in the gut.

title: Does Lead Harm the Developing Brain Through the Gut Microbiome?
desc: Animal and human cohort studies link lead exposure to gut microbiome dysbiosis, a candidate mediator of lead's neurodevelopmental harm via the gut-brain axis.

title: Mercury, Methylmercury, and the Microbiome: How Gut Microbes Shape Neurotoxic Risk
desc: How gut microbes methylate and demethylate mercury via hgcAB and merB, how mercury reshapes the microbiome, and why this shapes methylmercury neurotoxic risk.

title: The Metal-Microbiome-Disease Axis: How Heavy Metals May Drive Disease Through the Gut
desc: The metal-microbiome-disease axis: heavy-metal exposure reshapes the gut microbiome, and that dysbiosis may drive metabolic, neurological and gut disease.

title: How Low-Dose Heavy Metals May Reshape the Gut Microbiome to Drive Obesity
desc: Low-dose arsenic, cadmium, and lead may reshape the gut microbiome, depleting SCFA producers and promoting obesity and metabolic syndrome. Evidence examined.

title: Metals, the Microbiome, and Parkinson's: A Gut-First Pathway to Neurodegeneration
desc: How heavy-metal exposure may reshape the gut microbiome and feed gut-first alpha-synuclein pathology in Parkinson's disease - a metallomic-microbiome view.

title: How Dietary Nickel Arms Gut Bacteria — and May Fuel Gut Disease
desc: Dietary nickel activates nickel-dependent virulence enzymes in gut Enterobacteriaceae — a mechanistic pathway that may link nickel exposure to NEC and IBD.

title: Nitric Oxide Sensing by the [4Fe-4S] Regulator ArnR
desc: ArnR uses a [4Fe-4S] cluster to sense nitric oxide: NO nitrosylates the cluster, abolishing DNA binding and derepressing nitrate-respiration and hmp genes.

title: Arsenic Exposure Reshapes the Gut Microbiome of Bangladeshi Children, Enriching Resistance-Carrying E. coli
desc: Arsenic-exposed Bangladeshi children carry more gut Proteobacteria and E. coli bearing arsenic-resistance (ars) and antibiotic-resistance-like genes, a metal-microbiome case study.

title: Childhood Blood Metals and the Gut Microbiome: Evidence from the GESTE Cohort
desc: GESTE cohort links childhood blood metals (Mn, Se, Cd, Hg, Pb) to gut microbiome composition in 6-7 year olds; manganese and selenium tied to bacterial phyla.

title: Copper in Infectious Disease: Both Sides of the Penny
desc: How the immune system weaponizes copper against pathogens: macrophage copper bursts, phagosomal intoxication, fungal copper detox, and copper nutritional immunity.

title: A Multi-Omics + MR Enterography Model for Predicting Bowel Damage in Crohn's Disease
desc: Two-center study fusing gut microbiome, fecal and serum metabolomics, and MR enterography into a model predicting cumulative Crohn's bowel damage (AUC 0.857).

title: Gallium as an Iron Mimic: Disrupting Pseudomonas Iron Metabolism in Cystic Fibrosis
desc: Gallium substitutes for iron to sabotage Pseudomonas aeruginosa iron metabolism. A Phase 1 CF trial (Goss et al., Sci Transl Med 2018) found IV gallium improved lung function.

title: Gut Microbiome and Childhood Stunting in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
desc: Systematic review of 14 studies links childhood stunting in LMICs to inflammatory gut pathobionts and depleted butyrate producers, driving impaired linear growth.

title: The Human Microbiome Across Body Sites: Gut, Skin, Oral, Vaginal and Lung
desc: How the human microbiome differs across the gut, skin, oral, vaginal and lung niches, how it is acquired and disrupted, and why heavy-metal exposure matters.

title: Heavy Metals and the Gut Microbiota: A Systematic Review
desc: Systematic review of 12 human studies links arsenic, lead, mercury, and cadmium exposure to gut microbiota dysbiosis, leaky gut, and disease, with dietary mitigation.

title: Maternal Metallomic Profiles in Pregnancy with Obesity: A Secondary Analysis of UPBEAT
desc: UPBEAT analysis profiled 18 serum metals in 755 pregnant women with obesity: elevated manganese linked to antepartum haemorrhage, phosphorus to NICU care.

title: HERFD-XAS: High-Resolution X-ray Speciation of Biological Metals
desc: HERFD-XAS sharpens X-ray absorption spectra by rejecting core-hole broadening, resolving mercury, selenium, and arsenic speciation in dilute biological samples for metallomics.

title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Transfusion-Dependent Thalassemia
desc: Clinical review of deferoxamine, deferiprone, and deferasirox for transfusion iron overload in thalassemia, covering cardiac and hepatic iron outcomes measured by MRI T2*.

title: Iron Fortification, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Diarrhea Risk
desc: Iron fortification shifts the infant gut microbiome toward enterobacteria and pathogenic E. coli, cutting protective bifidobacteria and raising diarrhea risk.

title: Iron Fortification and the Kenyan Infant Gut Microbiome
desc: A full review of Jaeggi et al. (Gut 2015): iron-fortified porridge increased pathogenic E. coli and enterobacteria, cut bifidobacteria, and inflamed the gut in Kenyan infants.

title: The Iron Metalloproteome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Under Oxic and Anoxic Conditions
desc: Native metalloproteomics maps how Pseudomonas aeruginosa partitions iron across four protein complexes, with denitrification raising iron demand in anoxia.

title: Iron-Sulfur Clusters and Oxygen in Human Disease
desc: How iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster biogenesis and oxygen shape human disease: NFS1 in lung cancer, hyperoxia injury, and hypoxia therapy for Friedreich ataxia.

title: Iron Supplements and the Gut Microbiome in Reproductive-Age Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial
desc: A 21-day randomized placebo-controlled trial found ferrous fumarate did not significantly alter fecal microbiome composition in Australian reproductive-age women.

title: Iron- and Zinc-Biofortified Foods and the Gut Microbiota
desc: Systematic review of iron/zinc-biofortified bean and wheat diets in the Gallus gallus model: staples raised SCFA-producing Lactobacillus and cut enteric pathogens.

title: Lactobacillus plantarum 299v and Oral Iron Therapy Tolerance
desc: A randomized trial shows the probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum 299v reduces oral iron side effects and improves iron status in iron-deficiency anemia patients.

title: Lactoferrin vs. Ferrous Sulfate Through a Metallomics Lens
desc: Meta-analyses show oral lactoferrin can match or outperform ferrous sulfate for iron repletion, lowering IL-6 and hepcidin with fewer gut side effects.

title: Metal Availability and Immune Function During Infection
desc: How zinc, iron, manganese, and copper availability shapes neutrophil and macrophage function during infection through nutritional immunity, calprotectin, and phagosomal metal handling.

title: [NiFe]-Hydrogenase Cofactor Biosynthesis and the Hyp Maturation Proteins (HypA-F) in E. coli
desc: How E. coli builds the NiFe(CN)2CO cofactor of [NiFe]-hydrogenases: the HypA-F maturation proteins, cyanide and CO ligand synthesis, and nickel insertion.

title: Nutritional Immunity and Trace Metals in Infection
desc: How the host uses iron, zinc, manganese and copper handling as nutritional immunity to starve or poison pathogens, plus metal-based therapeutic strategies.

title: Intestinal Biomarkers and the Non-Motor Phenotype of Parkinson's Disease
desc: Parkinson's patients with constipation show higher fecal calprotectin, reduced SCFAs, lower gut diversity, and greater IBD genetic risk, linking gut inflammation to non-motor severity.

title: Pediatric Gut Microbiome Composition in Health: What a Systematic Review Reveals
desc: A systematic review of 42 studies finds geography, diet, and 16S sequencing method, not age, shape healthy children's Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes gut profiles.

title: Perinatal Tobacco Exposure Reshapes the Child Gut Microbiota
desc: A Spanish birth-cohort study found prenatal tobacco smoke, a source of cadmium and lead, lowers gut Akkermansia and raises Dorea in children by age 7.

title: Prebiotics Blunt the Gut Cost of Iron-Fortified Cereal in Kenyan Infants
desc: In a Kenyan infant RCT, adding prebiotic GOS/FOS to iron-fortified cereal raised iron absorption 60% and reduced gut inflammation, pathogens, and dysbiosis.

title: Prenatal Acetaminophen, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Cognition
desc: GESTE cohort links prenatal acetaminophen and caffeine to childhood gut microbiome shifts and cognition; Proteobacteria abundance modified WISC-IV scores.

title: Prenatal Lead Exposure and the Childhood Gut Microbiome
desc: Prenatal lead exposure is negatively linked to the childhood gut microbiome: metagenomics from a Mexico City cohort ties maternal Pb to fewer beneficial bacteria.

title: Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Intestinal Inflammation
desc: A 2024 PROGRESS cohort study links prenatal copper and cesium exposure, interacting with specific gut microbes, to elevated fecal calprotectin in children.

title: Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Depression
desc: A Mexico City birth-cohort study links a prenatal zinc-cobalt profile plus specific gut bacteria to 15.4% higher childhood depression scores at ages 9-11.

title: Spatial Metallomics in Colorectal Cancer: Copper-Immune and Iron-EMT Pathways
desc: Spatial metallomics pairs LA-ICP-TOF-MS with Visium transcriptomics in colorectal cancer, mapping copper to immune genes and iron to EMT at the tumor front.

title: Proteome-Scale Mapping of Iron-Binding Proteins in Bread Wheat
desc: A proteome-wide scan of bread wheat mapped ~600 iron-binding proteins with Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites coordinated by His, Glu, Asp and Cys, aiding metallomics.

title: The Zinc Clasp: How Zn2+ Shapes T-Cell Signaling
desc: The zinc clasp is a Zn2+-bridged interface that tethers the kinase Lck to CD4 and CD8 coreceptors, a labile-zinc switch central to T-cell activation and immunity.
